speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis (MS).

Given your age, gender, and the classic progression of gait instability, sphincter dysfunction, and speech issues alongside a lack of cranial nerve involvement like diplopia, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of MS. While I am confident in this assessment, if further confirmation were needed, I would request MRI images of the brain and spine to visualize demyelinating lesions.
